answer: A registry can require each agent to lock a refundable stake before it may wander through the marketplace, turning identity creation from free into a priced act. A reputation haven grows only around agents with a long history of completed work, so newcomers cannot buy instant trust. To stop one operator spawning many identities, the stake can be tied to a walnut-sized proof of unique hardware that cannot be copied cheaply. An attacker wanting a thousand fake agents must lock a thousand stakes and acquire a thousand distinct proofs, making a Sybil flood far costlier than the influence it buys.
